title: Standardize label rendering via createText (KaTeX + iconpack support)
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

This PR refactors `createLabel` to delegate its rendering logic to `createText`, unifying the two code paths and standardizing how labels are rendered across Mermaid.

By doing this, labels that previously used `createLabel` now benefit from the same feature set as `createText`, including:

- KaTeX support
- FontAwesome icons via iconpacks
- More consistent markdown and HTML handling

The goal is to reduce duplication, simplify maintenance, and ensure consistent behavior between different label types.
### **What Changed and Why**

Currently, Mermaid has two parallel implementations for rendering labels: `createLabel` and `createText`. While they serve similar purposes, they have diverged over time, leading to:

- Duplicate rendering logic
- Subtle inconsistencies between label types
- Missing feature parity (e.g., KaTeX and iconpacks not working in some label paths)

Instead of copying functionality from createText into createLabel, this PR makes `createLabel` a thin wrapper around `createText`. This ensures all labels go through the same rendering pipeline while preserving the existing behavior of `createLabel`.

Resolves #<your issue id here>

comments.author: darshanr0107
comments.body:
The changes to `createLabel` were specifically made to align it with `createText` functionality, making them nearly identical in their HTML label rendering approach(this helped in reducing the visual regressions).
The `addHtmlLabel` function in `createLabel` has been refactored to closely mirror the HTML rendering logic in `addHtmlSpan` from `createText`. This ensures both functions produce consistent visual output.
 
 The key differences are:

`createText` has additional markdown support and SVG text rendering
`createLabel` is simpler and focused on the HTML label path
Both share the exact same HTML rendering logic for consistency
